 The proposal suggests increasing the student loan amount to 10 million VND per person per month, with an interest rate of 4.8% per year.
 The Ministry of Education and Training has proposed increasing the maximum student loan amount to 10 million VND per person per month with a preferential interest rate of 4.8% per year, in the context of total outstanding loans to students and postgraduate students reaching nearly 25,000 billion VND.
 Báo Tiền Phong • 25/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 According to the Ministry of Education and Training, in the 2025-2026 academic year, student loan programs will continue to support disadvantaged students in maintaining their studies and expanding their access to higher education .
 As of May 31, 2026, the student loan program under Decision 157/2007/QD-TTg and Decision 05/2022/QD-TTg recorded a total outstanding loan balance of VND 24,475 billion, with 355,805 customers currently borrowing funds.
 Meanwhile, the credit policy for students, master's students, and doctoral candidates in science , technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields, according to Decision 29/2025/QD-TTg, has outstanding loans of VND 422.9 billion, with 6,272 customers currently borrowing funds.
 You may also like The total outstanding debt of the two programs reached nearly VND 24,898 billion, with 362,077 customers still having outstanding loans. The new credit policy has expanded support to postgraduate training and STEM fields, contributing to the development of human resources in priority areas. 
 Candidates taking the 2026 high school graduation exam. For the 2026-2027 academic year, the Ministry of Education and Training will continue to propose to the Prime Minister adjustments to the student loan policy to address practical shortcomings. Notably, the Ministry proposes increasing the maximum loan amount to 10 million VND/month/student, researching the application of a preferential interest rate of 4.8%/year, and connecting data between the Social Policy Bank, training institutions, and relevant agencies. The Ministry also proposes improving the mechanism for adjusting loan terms and extending repayment periods for borrowers facing objective difficulties after graduation.
 You may also like In implementing Resolution 71-NQ/TW and Resolution 281/NQ-CP, the Ministry of Education and Training advised the Government to issue Decree 317/2026/ND-CP dated August 11, 2026, on the organization, management, and use of the National Scholarship Fund. The Decree takes effect from October 1, 2026, creating a basis for mobilizing resources for the identification, nurturing of talent, and development of high-quality human resources.
 According to the Ministry of Education and Training, while scholarship, grant, and social funding sources are quite diverse, they are also fragmented. The Ministry stated that there is a need for unified guidance on the management, transparency, and accounting of these support funds, while also limiting the situation where one person receives support from multiple sources.
